newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel rejects PLO accusations on closure.
newsitem.headline: Israel rejects PLO accusations on closure.

text.p: The Israeli army on Friday denied that closing the border with the Gaza Strip had prevented sick Palestinians from receiving adequate medical treatment.
Palestinian Health Minister Riyad al-Zaanoun said on Thursday that a 95-year-old Gazan woman died of a blood clot because she, like others, could not get past Israeli roadblocks for hospital care.
He said the woman was one of five people to die for lack of help but he offered no further evidence.

Friday's army statement made no reference to any specific cases but quoted Colonel Dov Tsadka, in charge of the liaison unit at the Erez border crossing, as saying such claims were "Palestinian propaganda".
Tsadka said that since the closure some 100 sick Palestinians had been allowed out of Gaza for medical treatment.
Israel closed its borders to Palestinians and confined them to their home towns in the West Bank and Gaza Strip after a twin suicide bombing killed 13 people in a Jerusalem market last week.
An Israeli military official said on Thursday that Israel would allow the transfer of about 20 truckloads of food, medicine, animal feed and other essentials into Gaza on Friday.
The Israeli army said on Friday it was easing the internal closure around Nablus and Jericho in the West Bank but kept up roadblocks around other towns in that territory.
Nablus residents said roadblocks in the area had been eased but buses taking Palestinians to the Jordanian border were still being held up in Jericho.
The Palestinian Authority in charge of self-rule areas set up under interim Israel-PLO peace deals calls the closure collective punishment.
Zaanoun said on Thursday: "I wonder how Jews who suffered collective punishment from the Nazis can practise such punishments on the Palestinian people."
